document.title: Ariana Afghan Airlines: Assets and Activities (OTI IR 1999-170CX)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: OTI intelligence report on the assets and activities of Ariana Afghan Airlines. Cited in 9/11 Commission Report Chapter 2, Endnote 77.

organizations.name: Ariana Afghan Airlines
organizations.notes: Afghanistan's national carrier, founded 1955. The Taliban took operational control in September 1996 and retain de facto ownership. Used for military transport, drug smuggling and terrorist movements.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Controls Ariana and earns overflight fees; uses the airline for troop and supply transport in the civil war.

organizations.name: Indamer
organizations.notes: Indian firm that helped finance Ariana in 1955 and owned 49 percent; its shares were later bought by Pan American Airlines.

organizations.name: Pan American Airlines
organizations.notes: Bought Indamer's shares in Ariana. The text reads 'American Airlines', with a marginal 'P' preceding it that suggests Pan Am.

organizations.name: Bakhtar Afghan Airlines
organizations.notes: Took over the company in 1985 to become the national airline; the Ariana name was restored in 1988.

organizations.name: Air France
organizations.notes: Held a technical support contract with Ariana, which was being re-negotiated in June 1997.

organizations.name: Sabena
organizations.notes: Brussels-based airline that Ariana considered for a technical relationship in mid-1997.

organizations.name: Royal Jordanian
organizations.notes: Amman-based airline that reportedly signed an aircraft service agreement with Ariana.

organizations.name: Boeing
organizations.notes: Held spare-parts talks with Ariana from mid-1998, with at least two deliveries.

organizations.name: International Air Transport Association
organizations.notes: Calculates the $400 overflight fee and holds the fees in trust in Switzerland.

organizations.name: International Committee of the Red Cross
organizations.notes: Operates its own flights into Afghanistan.

organizations.name: United Nations
organizations.notes: Operates its own flights into Afghanistan.

organizations.name: Government of Pakistan
organizations.notes: Signed an October 1996 technical support agreement giving Ariana a temporary base at Karachi.

organizations.name: Government of Saudi Arabia
organizations.notes: Reportedly stopped the Jeddah leg of Ariana flights from October 1998.

places.name: Afghanistan
places.significance: Base of Ariana and the Taliban; subject of overflight fees.

places.name: Kabul
places.significance: Where Ariana was founded in 1955 and which the Taliban captured in September 1996; site of the international airport.

places.name: Amritsar
places.significance: Thrice-weekly Ariana Boeing 727 service, mainly carrying consumer goods.

places.name: United Arab Emirates
places.significance: Islamic extremists flew Ariana there in 1997; also a route for illicit money.

places.name: Jeddah
places.significance: Weekly Ariana destination, halted at Saudi behest from October 1998.

places.name: Karachi
places.significance: Temporary Ariana operational and maintenance base under the October 1996 agreement.

places.name: Frankfurt
places.significance: Charter service for a German NGO.

events.description: Ariana Afghan Airlines was founded in Kabul with financial help from Indamer.
Bakhtar Afghan Airlines took over the company and the Ariana name was dropped; it was restored in 1988.
The Taliban captured Kabul and took operational control of Ariana.
Technical support agreement with Pakistan gave Ariana a temporary operational and maintenance base at Karachi.
The Air France technical support contract was being re-negotiated because it had become too expensive.
Members of an Islamic extremist group flew Ariana from Afghanistan to the UAE.
The Jeddah leg was reportedly stopped at the behest of the Saudi Government.
Talks on spare parts acquisition began between Ariana and Boeing around mid-1998, with deliveries including one in early February 1999.
Ariana Afghan Airlines founded in Kabul with financial help from Indamer.
Afghanistan signed the Air Transport Development Project Agreement with the US; Pan American later bought Indamer's shares.
Ariana name dropped as Bakhtar Afghan Airlines took over; name restored in 1988.
Taliban captured Kabul and took operational control of Ariana.
Technical support agreement with Pakistan gave Ariana a temporary base at Karachi.
Ariana–Air France technical support contract being renegotiated as too expensive.
Ariana explored technical relationship with Sabena (mid-1997).
Talks on spare parts between Ariana and Boeing began in mid-1998.
Ariana's Jeddah flights reportedly halted at Saudi Government behest.
Boeing spare parts delivery to Ariana in early February 1999.
CIA Office of Transnational Issues issued the intelligence report on Ariana Afghan Airlines.

key_claims: Ariana provides the Taliban with unspecified profits from its legitimate passenger, cargo and charter services.
Ariana has facilitated activity by terrorists and narcotics traffickers.
Usama bin Ladin frequently chartered Ariana Boeing 727s to move supplies and personnel.
The Taliban have made clear that Ariana's first priority is helping Kabul win the civil war, and the airline is frequently tasked to transport troops and supplies.
The Taliban earn about $11.7 million annually in overflight fees, banked in Switzerland and restricted to civil aviation use.
Heroin and opium are frequently smuggled from Afghanistan aboard Ariana aircraft.
